column1: # Format (UTF-8, tab separated, `#` starts a comment):
# This file is original work authored for this project and is covered by the
# repository LICENSE. Unlike data\LekhoniCore.merged.bgk, it may be
# redistributed. A phrase entry outranks the core dictionary and the
# transliteration when the whole word has been typed, so it is the supported
# way to correct a spelling without regenerating the core dictionary.
# Keep the list short and purposeful: names, brand spellings, and words the
# general corpus renders differently. See data\README.md for the dictionary
# format and the redistribution rules for the core dictionary.
# Words whose correct spelling differs from the phonetic conversion.
# Words where a general rule would be wrong, or where a core dictionary key
# disagrees with the spelling this project ships.
# nya is ন্য (n + its own phala). The merged core stores the letter name ঞ
# under the exact key "nya", so the rule table cannot win here; the phrase
# layer outranks the core dictionary and is the supported override.
# shunno is শুন্য: `nn` takes the n-phala and the final o stays inherent. The
# inherent-o rule cannot see that an earlier vowel in the same word already
# claimed the syllable, so the word is listed rather than the heuristic.
# kokkho is কক্ষ. Listed as one word only, because `kkh` must stay ক্খ: a bare
# `k` followed by `kh` really is ক্ + খ, and collapsing that to ক্ষ would
# break every other kh word. Revisit only with a decision on `ksh` vs `kkh`.
# noya is নয়া with the long o. The merged core has an exact key "noya" that
# stores নয়, so the rule table's নয়া loses to it and the phrase has to win.
# Next-word predictions. The fourth column is a pipe-separated local list shown
# after the previous word is committed. The merged core dictionary carries no
# prediction lists at all, so without these the prediction feature does nothing
# in a shipped build; see docs/TEST_PLAN.md and the audit suite, which reports
# how many entries a given image actually has.
# These are deliberately few and high-frequency. Predictions are a local hint,
# not a language model, so a short accurate list beats a long noisy one.
